output: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter flew very close to a US RC-135U aircraft carrying out a routine mission in the Sea of Okhotsk, demonstrating its weapons by maneuvering aggressively and exposing missiles to the American pilots. This incident occurred amid heightened tensions between the US and Russia over Russia's involvement in Ukraine, as expressed by the condemnation of Russian "aggression" by President Barack Obama earlier in the month and a previous aggressive incident involving a Russian fighter jet over a US Navy destroyer in the Black Sea.

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour to celebrate Charles' 67th birthday, visiting 12 different towns and cities across Australia and New Zealand, marking his 15th visit to Australia, with a possible meeting with the Australian Prime Minister.
A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, on September 20, while a man was detained and questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station following an incident on a subsequent day.
Hugh McGoldrick, a former GP, had his name removed from the medical register after admitting falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients, as no appeal was submitted within the 28-day deadline.
A 21-year-old is under police questioning on suspicion of murder, after a body was found in a wooded area in Dorking, Surrey, and the post-mortem results are pending.

Josh Hanson was stabbed and died at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, around 1:10 BST on Sunday. Police are appealing for anyone who was in the bar after midnight or in the nearby area around 1:00 AM to come forward with information, as no arrests have been made in the case.

The article discusses a potential new service between Sandown and Southsea, aimed at boosting tourism to the Isle of Wight, with the possibility of the service operating two days a week in July and August, subject to permits and further discussions.
A 30-year-old man was arrested following an attack by up to eight individuals on a victim in the Heights area at around 2 AM BST on Sunday, with police appealing for information about the incident.

In India, floods have caused the death of over 200 people in Assam, affected 450,000, and displaced many more. The Prime Minister plans to visit Assam to find a permanent solution to the annual flooding problem in the region.

The 25th anniversary season of the Premier League starts with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on Friday 11 August, with Sky Sports holding the rights to broadcast 10 Friday night matches, while a significant portion of football fans reported using unofficial online streams for matches.

Footballer Cristian Montano, aged 22, was dismissed by Oldham Athletic after a spot-fixing investigation by the National Crime Agency resulted in his arrest and suspension, a move deemed essential by the club in order to act swiftly and seriously.

In June 2014, a former Pontins resort at Brixham was destroyed by a fire started "for fun" by 20-year-old Rick Edwards. Edwards was sentenced to a suspended jail term and a year's supervision order. The fire caused extensive damage and increased the final cost of demolition due to the presence of asbestos.

Scottish athlete Robert Wilson, 30, returned to Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in 2013 for a second stint that spanned 51 appearances, but has remained without a team since his release in May 2023. Prior to his return to Forest, Wilson had previously played at Preston North End and Notts County.

Australia left-arm seamer Faulkner took 3 wickets (3-45) including key dismissals of Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, and Thisara Perera, while debutant Sri Lankan slow left-armer Amila Aponso shone with 4-18 as Sri Lanka made 288 in Colombo. After Matthew Wade scored 76, Australia was bowled out for 206 in reply, resulting in an 82-run win for Sri Lanka, leveling the five-match bilateral series at 1-1.

The 32-year-old rugby player Vadim Cobilas, the first Moldova international to play in the Premiership, is leaving Sale and moving to France's Top 14, with his position set to be filled by advanced talks with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings, while some other players are considering their own futures.

India, cruising towards their highest successful run-chase in Australia with consecutive centuries from Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli, suffered a dramatic collapse from 277-1 to 323 all out due to Kane Richardson's 5-68, with India losing the match and the series 4-0 to Australia, who also sealed an 18th consecutive one-day win on home soil.

The Hammersmith and City Line and sections of the Circle Line were temporarily suspended due to potential debris falling on the tracks, requested by the London Fire Brigade following a fire in a 24-story block, where currently it is presumed that 58 people have died, with the lines anticipated to reopen once the debris is secured.

Veteran Footballer Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old who has previously played for Kilmarnock, returns to the club after a three-year stint at Hearts, marking his 150th appearance for Kilmarnock with a new three-year contract.
Ross Morgan, an excited Ipswich fan, accidentally punched a hole in the ceiling while celebrating Paul Anderson's goal against Norwich, with Anderson later offering to cover the repair costs.

Retailers in Wales are now compelled to hide tobacco products from public view, with fines and imprisonment possible for violations, in an effort to reduce visual access and thus discourage smoking, a decision backed by Public Health Wales.

The 20-year-old footballer named Lucas, who has previously played for the National League side and scored three goals in 10 appearances, is brought into the Bristol Rovers squad in League Two, with manager Luke Garrard suggesting he will provide options in the forward areas.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovation, including waterproofing and removal/rebuild of the chimney stack on the signal box, with work primarily conducted at night to reduce disruption. The station, rich in history, is operated by Northern Rail.
Former NFL player Lawrence Phillips, known for his troubles both on and off the field, is believed to have committed suicide while serving a prison term for murder accusations.

The article discusses the extension of bus lane hours for Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT), starting at 7:00 and ending at 19:00, and a plan for two rounds of public consultation to design the system, considering factors like loading and unloading windows, to ensure efficient and user-friendly service, with operation scheduled to begin in September 2018.

Argentinian football star Lionel Messi scored the winning goal for Barcelona in La Liga, surpassing the record as the competition's all-time top scorer, while coincidentally Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo also claimed the record title for his club's record league scorer the same day.

Over 70 individuals, including football players and directors from 30 clubs in lower Italian leagues, have been detained for allegations of "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud," with links to mafia organizations such as the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and a local police officer is also under investigation in the ongoing probe led by the Catanzaro prosecutors.

Researchers released 1,600 hybrid spiderlings (Dolomedes plantarius) from a cross-breed of species from Sussex and Suffolk into suitable dykes at Castle Marshes, aiming to increase genetic variability, potentially enhancing the new spider population's ability to adapt to its surroundings and climate change impacts, funded by the BBC Wildlife Fund.

The Partition of India in 1947 led to the formation of two new independent countries (Pakistan and Bangladesh), and the displacement of millions, including the story of a woman and her familyshared in the Newsround special "Finding My Family - Partition" on CBBC.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner who participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, attempted her 20th marathon, completing approximately 14 miles before deciding to take an Underground train to Westminster and walking the rest of the route. Despite not completing the full distance, she expressed joy over the experience and no regrets about participating.

In China's top cities, the extreme competition in the property market has prompted some couples to resort to fake divorces to purchase additional homes, as the central bank's attempts to curb prices have had limited impact on affordability for young workers with low wages.

A 24-year-old individual is under arrest in connection with the suspicious death of Mr. Jones, a landlord, following a confrontation at a public house in Holyhead. The police are investigating and have released a family statement about Mr. Jones, who is described as a partner, soulmate, father, brother, and uncle. A post-mortem examination was conducted, but the cause of death has not been released yet. The police have requested information from individuals who were on a specific bus that passed through the Black Bridge area of Holyhead at the time of the incident.
The article invites readers to connect with BBC News Entertainment through various social media platforms, and encourages them to submit their story suggestions to a specific email address.

A red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided on the A713 near Carsphairn, causing the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka and Scott Kennedy, who were from Ayrshire. Police are investigating and are particularly interested in a white flat-bed pickup truck that was on the road at the time of the crash.

Australian rowing champion Sarah Tait, who won a silver medal at the 2012 London Olympics with Kate Hornsey, was diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, serving as an inspiration to many young athletes in Australia, particularly female rowers. Heather Stanning, her British competitor from the Olympics, described Tait as an "incredible personality" and an inspiration for women in sports worldwide.

On the day after the signing of a deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan, Taliban bombed two buses in Kabul, resulting in injuries for soldiers and civilians, as well as a shopkeeper witnessing the aftermath of the first attack. The Taliban claimed responsibility for the attacks, which they described as a continuation of their offensive, that started in the summer.

Daimler predicts significant growth in full-year sales, despite a slowdown in Mercedes sales in China, with confidence in continued growth in major emerging markets, although at a lower rate than last year, and a 6% increase in car and commercial vehicle sales in Q2.

A 10-year-old Danish prince was rescued from a dangerous rip current at Mermaid Beach by lifeguard Nick Malcolm, who could have prevented the boy's potential death, according to his supervisor Stuart Keay.
Emergency services responded to a nonsuspicious house fire where an elderly man's body was discovered on Elgin Road at 16:10 on Wednesday. No others were injured.

Veterans with complex amputation-related medical issues in the UK are now receiving treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, following the implementation of a system enabling tertiary referrals from NHS centers, leveraging the DMRC's decade-long expertise in managing military trauma injuries, thereby ensuring these veterans receive the highest quality care for their sacrifices.

Four speed enforcement cameras installed on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot, Wales, have resulted in about 125 daily violations in less than a week, a decrease from the 700 daily violations during a trial period in December. The cameras serve as a deterrent to excessive speeding, but focus is on education rather than penalties.

A Manchester-born teacher living in Spain is under arrest for secretly taking and storing explicit photos of his underage students, some of which were shared online, as part of an Interpol investigation into illegal activities involving minors. Police are now trying to identify the victims in the images found on his electronic devices.

A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, once displayed at World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire, survived a flood and was later found at a nearby car wash. The center's manager reported the fish, which can sell for up to £1,000, had some scrapes but was otherwise healthy and eager to return to its display.

Chris Rock, the comedian and actor, has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak, after 19 years of marriage, focusing on their family privacy; they share two daughters, the latest film starring Rock is a comedy about a comedian bystander in his own reality TV wedding.

A collision occurred on the motorway between Tamnamore, causing it to be shut down in both directions, resulting in significant traffic delays. Drivers traveling to Belfast are advised to exit at junction 15, while those heading to Enniskillen in County Fermanagh should exit at junction 12 and use Armagh city as an alternative route. Witnesses of the crash or those who saw the involved Honda Civic before the incident are asked to contact the police with information.

The French government has proposed senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini for the role of ambassador to the Vatican, aiming to improve relations with the more tolerant Pope Francis, but the Vatican has yet to respond or confirm the nomination, which is being viewed as a potential rejection due to the silence typically maintained by the Vatican in such cases.

The Nasdaq fell 2.4%, marking its biggest one-day drop since April 2020, driven by declines in semiconductor, biotech, and other tech stocks, despite a 35% rise in Kraft Foods after it agreed to merge with Heinz. Additionally, the Dow Jones and S&P 500 also dropped significantly, while the US dollar weakened against the euro due to a decline in US durable goods orders.

Two underdogs had memorable victories in tennis tournaments: Marketa Vondrousova, the Czech world number 233, moved closer to the top 100 for the first time by beating Estonia's Kontaveit and Barbora Strycova to win a women's event. In the men's Grand Prix Hassan II, 20-year-old Borna Coric of Croatia rallied from behind to beat Germany's Philipp Kohlschreiber and claim his first ATP title.
Stoke City signs Cameroon International and former Schalke player, Eric Choupo-Moting, their fourth transfer of the summer, after a prolonged interest that dates back to 2016.

A man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, passed away at a nursing home last September, but it was not till April of this year that his death was classified as a murder, leading to a woman being questioned by police.

Heavy rains have resulted in severe waterlogging, causing a city-wide standstill, school and office closures, and affected around 80,000 people in Sri Lanka, while triggering evacuations and rescues in India's Tamil Nadu state, with the chief minister announcing a relief fund for flood-affected areas, noting the unusually Heavy rainfall within a short period.

A McGill's 904 bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, with the driver successfully evacuating all passengers without injury, as mentioned by one grateful passenger whose partially-sighted mother was on board. The road was closed, but it was later reopened after the burnt-out bus was removed.

Notts County's 25-year-old bowler, Jake Ball, is the leading wicket-taker in Division One of the County Championship in 2016 with 12 wickets in two games, including a six-wicket haul in each, demandingly leading the bowling attack alongside Stuart Broad and praised by Mick Newell and Peter Moores for his form and potential progression within the ECB setup. However, despite Ball's performance, Notts lost their second County Championship match against Lancashire by eight wickets.

A memorial stone made of Jersey granite, dedicated to the 120 "Jersey Pals" who were killed during the Battle of the Somme, was officially unveiled in the French village of Guillemont. A core was removed from the memorial and will be returned to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square, serving as a permanent reminder of Jersey's role in World War I.

John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and was a member of Theatre Peckham's company from age nine to 14, is currently filming Star Wars Episode Eight and expressed his honor to give back to the theatre, with its founder noting he will be a great inspiration for the young members.

In the European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat holds a one-shot lead with a birdie at the 14th, while Fitzpatrick, who led since day one, matches him with a birdie at the 15th. Donald, former world number one, scores a 65 and is four behind, while Westwood is two shots more back after a 67. Several players, including Donald, are within five strokes of the lead, with Welshman Bradley Dredge withdrawing due to illness.

In a turnaround for Middlesex, Ashton Agar Voges and Dawid Malan put on a 279-run third-wicket partnership, with Voges scoring his first century of the season (128*), despite losing Malan (147) to Liam Dawson, leaving Middlesex in a strong position for their first County Championship win of the season, while Hampshire remain hopeful of a draw, given unfavorable weather forecast.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically ill in hospital following an incident on Penilee Road, while police located a man they previously wanted to speak to in the Dumfries and Galloway area, and forensic investigations are ongoing at the scene.

The three-bedroom red brick terrace house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, once lived in by John Lennon from birth to age five, was sold to an anonymous bidder through a bidding war for an undisclosed amount, exceeding its guide price of £150,000 to £250,000, with significant interest from local and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, 29, denied owning a dog that attacked and eventually resulted in the death of David Ellam, 52, while walking his Yorkshire terrier last August in Sheepridge, Huddersfield. Joseph was bailed and the trial has been set for February 5, with a possible earlier trial date in hopes of the Recorder of Leeds, Judge Peter Collier QC. Joseph also pleaded guilty to possessing cannabis on the same day.
Twenty-two-year-old Thomas Bebbington, last seen entering a river near Dana Steps, was later found deceased, approximately 10 miles away from Shrewsbury.

Five-week-old otter cubs, unable to survive independently, are currently being cared for and fed multiple times daily, with hopes they'll mature enough to move to a spacious outdoor enclosure with live food during the summer.

A 33-year-old mother of four named Joanne Thompson was found dead at her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards on Wednesday, and police are investigating, requesting witnesses to a Monday bonfire disturbance, as well as anyone who saw activity around her house on Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking number of 2,270 black-tailed godwits restocked in a small field in Kilmoluaig, Hebrides, this spring, with a significant portion coming from Europe (France, Portugal, Spain), and bystanders reported that many were on their way to Iceland for breeding.

Rangers coach Jimmy Durrant will not be renewing his contract at Ibrox, as manager Mark Warburton plans to shake up the coaching staff, given Durrant's history at the club spanning 14 years as a player and coach, including roles with the first team under Walter Smith and Ally McCoist.
A rare albino deer is reported, estimated to occur once in 100,000 births, generating visitor interest as it adjusts to its new environment.

A 15-year-old boy named Asad Khan from Bradford died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heath School, with his mother alleging he was bullied. During the inquest, it was revealed that Asad had expressed feelings of unsafe and thoughts to skip school, as well as comments about life being unfair. The coroner is considering calling a boy who may have information related to the case. The full inquest will resume next month.

The 1654 coronation ceremony painting, which has been hanging in Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle since 1880, is unique and valuable, but its origins and the artist responsible for its creation remain a mystery.

Macclesfield Town beat Wrexham 3-0, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker, placing them seventh in the table, while Wrexham remain 15th. Notable player actions include a yellow card for Curtis Tilt and Jordan Evans, and several substitutions on both sides.

The African Football Confederation (Caf) has agreed a sponsorship deal with French oil and gas company Total, marking Total's takeover from Orange as the headline sponsor for the next phase of 10 Caf competitions, aiming to further the development of African football and strengthen Total's ties to stakeholders and customers in Africa.

Spain coach Lopetegui has recalled veterans Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while goalkeeper David de Gea, defenders Sergio Ramos, Dani Carvajal, Gerard Pique, Jordi Alba, Marc Bartra, Cesar Azpilicueta, Javi Martinez, and midfielders Sergi Roberto, Sergio Busquets, Saul Niguez, Koke, Marco Asensio, Lucas Vazquez, Thiago Alcantara, David Silva, and Juan Mata are included in the squad for the World Cup qualifier against Liechtenstein and a friendly with Belgium. Final roster includes three goalkeepers (De Gea, Pepe Reina, Adrian), eight defenders (Ramos, Carvajal, Pique, Alba, Bartra, Azpilicueta, Martinez, and Javi Martinez), six midfielders (Sergi Roberto, Busquets, Saul Niguez, Koke, Asensio, Vazquez, Alcantara, Silva, Mata), and four forwards (Paco Alcacer, Nolito, Morata,

A wildfire, considered deliberate and spanning a 5-kilometer area across the border, is being fought by multiple fire services, with dozens of firefighters on the scene. This is the latest out of 435 wildfires since early May, and officials are urging the public to stop intentionally setting fires due to the risks to lives, property, and the countryside.

Ireland cricketer Boyd Rankin, 31, returns to the national team after a hiatus, citing a lack of opportunities with England in the last two years, and expressed eagerness for the chance to contribute to Ireland's potential bid for Test status as the World Twenty20 approaches.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, initiated by the Patient Client Council, seeks to provide an independent voice for sufferers and their carers of rare diseases, with a focus on education, special services, and support, aiming to advocate on their behalf and enhance treatment and care.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to open its choral group to girls for the first time, aiming to find talented youth from diverse backgrounds, and encouraging participation through an open day and auditions.

Chelsea winger Pedro, age 29, was hospitalized after sustaining an injury in the 3-0 win against Beijing, suffered a concussion, and required overnight stay. He is expected to wear a protective mask during training, with the Chelsea squad now in Singapore for upcoming matches against Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.

Former England cricketer James Taylor (27), who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, is now working with Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire's academies, offering one-day cricket experiences to their batsmen. Additionally, former Northants captain David Sales, who is known for his impressive batting statistics, is working with Nottinghamshire's batsmen, focusing on improving technical aspects of their game based on his cricket brain and experience.

A man was charged with multiple offenses, including assault and criminal damage, after an incident on Whiterock Road that was witnessed by people picking up prescriptions, including children, and was due to appear in court on December 5.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, prompting a volunteer crew from Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats in good weather conditions. They successfully towed the yacht to Carrick Marina, showcasing the effective coordination between the inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

In the match between Ipswich and MK Dons, David McGoldrick scored his first goal since August, Brett Pitman and Kane Vincent-Young extended Ipswich's lead, only for Chuks Aneke (Revell) to score twice from the spot and a free-kick, and Jarvis pounded in the winning header for Ipswich. Both managers, Mick McCarthy and Karl Robinson, reflect on an exciting but frustrating game, with MK Dons having a challenging overall season.

A pedestrian bridge collapsed on a London-bound motorway near Maidstone on August 27, causing serious injury to one motorcyclist, resulting in a man from Darlington facing multiple charges, including dangerous driving, and the road was closed twice for debris removal, affecting the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover.

Holidaymakers in Platja d'Aro were seized with panic after a flashmob consisting of individuals pretending to be paparazzi caused a stampede, mistaking selfie sticks for weapons. Police were called, resulting in eleven injuries and three hospitalizations, with organizers, German women, being detained for public order offences.

Two individuals, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, are charged with the murder of a 2.5-year-old boy, Jeremiah Regis, from Wolverhampton, who died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma. The court heard that Jeremiah had over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest.

A gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon spread over a large area due to high winds, resulting in four people being treated for smoke inhalation, one being hospitalized with burns, and triggering an overnight response from fire services. Evacuations were conducted at the nearby Woodbury Park Golf and Country Club, and the public was advised to avoid the area.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association has reached an agreement to secure the club's future, including a 15-year lease for the Beaumont Park venue, according to Keith Chapman, the chairman, with further meetings planned to establish management structure, schedule a 2017 race night, and other arrangements.

A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, died three days after being badly injured at Bobby Jones Place in St Andrews, and her 51-year-old brother, Charles Gordon, has been charges with her murder. The Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC) has ordered an investigation into the initial police response before the incident, focusing on the police's handling of the call-out to Ms Bowe's home, with a report to be submitted to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS) in due course.

A 29-year-old footballer, Jim O'Brien, has signed a two-year deal with Ross County after a brief loan period last season, where he made 18 appearances and scored twice. His return is hoped to provide valuable experience to the younger players and contribute to the team's development, although his international clearance could influence his participation in the upcoming Scottish League Cup match against Hibernian.

In Division Two cricket, Northants seized early advantages against Durham with regular wickets, dismissing top scorer Michael Richardson, Paul Collingwood, Keaton Jennings, and others for the low total of 103. Despite a fightback by Durham's Barry McCarthy, Northants ended the day struggling at 59-3, 107 runs behind. Durham's fragile batting lineup was exposed by Northants' seam attack after their recent dramatic defeat by Glamorgan.

A 19-year-old New Zealander trails by one shot the joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim after two rounds at the Sahalee Country Club by two-under, with Catriona Matthew three behind at one-over, on a difficult day marked by early sunshine, cool temperatures, and rain; only five players, including Henderson, remain under par at the halfway stage of the second women's major of the year.

Former footballer Steve Watson, 56, will rejoin Scotland's coaching staff as assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, having formerly worked under Alex McLeish during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign. Watson, who played with Strachan and Mark McGhee at Aberdeen, expressed enthusiasm for the opportunity to help Scotland in their World Cup qualifiers. He had previously left his position with Scotland after more than three years to take over as manager of Bradford City.

The article summarizes a hockey match between Belfast Giants and Braehead Clan, where Belfast Giants took a 4-1 lead and are in control of the game, with Alex Foster and Steve Saviano leading the team in scoring. The Giants have a game in hand on the Devils, and their next game is against Manchester Storm, while Braehead Clan will play the Giants again on 2nd January.

Jordan Spieth, the defending Masters champion, suffered a dramatic collapse on the final day of the tournament, culminating in a quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th. Danny Willett capitalized on this, becoming the first Englishman since Nick Faldo in 1996 to win the event. Faldo, a three-time Masters winner, described Spieth's collapse as a scarring and damaging experience, noting similarities with Greg Norman's collapse in 1996.

The article details instructions on how to submit photographs to England's Big Picture project by email, social media, or Instagram, emphasizing the use of recent images, adherence to BBC's Terms and Conditions, and retaining the copyright to submitted content while granting the BBC a non-exclusive license to use the materials.

Eye specialist Honey Rose is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter, accused of failing to detect serious swollen optic discs during a routine eye test on Vincent Barker (Vinnie), leading to his untimely death five months later.

Food price inflation increased to 4.9% in June, primarily due to rising pork prices, remaining below the target figure of 3.5%, and this might impede potential interest rate cuts in 2013 due to economic concerns and the risk of fueling a property bubble. The anticipated growth rate for China's economy in 2013 is expected to be 7.5%, which would be the slowest rate in 23 years.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away following a collapse during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on 5 June. His memorial service was attended by friends, family, and former team-mates, including Senegal striker Papiss Cisse, who shared a close bond with him. Known for his seven years at Newcastle United, Tiote made over 150 appearances during his tenure.

In the fifth stage of the race, Slovak rider Peter Sagan won the uphill sprint, with Thibaut Pinot moving to second overall, while Nairo Quintana maintained the lead. British rider Geraint Thomas moved up to sixth overall, with two stages remaining.
Cuadrilla secures approval for its fracking plans in Lancashire, promising local jobs, investment, and community benefits, but opponents have initiated a legal challenge.

Three 17-year-old and 19-year-old males from north-west London, initially missing over concerns they were planning to travel to Syria, were stopped and arrested on their return to the UK. They were later released without charge. Previously, three east London schoolgirls had disappeared, feared to have traveled to Istanbul and then on to Syria to join Islamic State (IS) militants.

A respiratory consultant, Dr. Christopher Davies, criticism a hospital's expenditure on purchasing a blackout blind for £22.95, stating it was fitted for free by in-house staff, while a hospital spokesperson stated the quote was reviewed and rejected, leading to a review of the situation by NHS England.

Adam King was instrumental in Swansea City's 2-0 win over Reading in March, and the Swans' development squad clinched the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, achieving 31 wins throughout the 2016-17 season, while the senior team was able to stay in the Premier League despite Hull's relegation due to Crystal Palace's 4-0 victory over them on Sunday.

December 2013 storms damaged a dune system east of Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, with natural re-establishment observed but concerns remain due to narrowness. The Denbighshire council is considering creating a secondary dune system to strengthen defenses against flooding, following a flood risk management report suggesting discussions with Natural Resources Wales to potentially create a secondary dune system on the landward side of the existing dunes. Approximately 400 residents were displaced from their homes in Rhyl, one of the hardest-hit areas, where hundreds of properties lost power during the storm.

South Shields (8th tier of English football), who successfully played at Wembley last season, will host a live FA Cup game against Bridlington Town, streamed across BBC Sport's digital platforms on August 19, with commentary from Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, who will interact with the audience via the #bbcfacup hashtag.

Police are investigating a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road, where a 38-year-old man suffered serious, but non-life threatening, facial injuries, while a 49-year-old man did not require medical attention. Police Scotland is asking for witnesses and information about any suspicious behavior or vehicles in the area around the time of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter after the death of 44-year-old Jonathan Baines, known as "Willy," at a house on Ropery Road, Gainsborough, following an outing to Market Rasen races and town pubs, and will be sentenced on December 21 at Lincoln Crown Court.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked by a couple in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries including an eye injury, and lost his mobile phone in the incident. The assault occurred on a 23:05 service between Glasgow Central and Neilston, with witnesses urged to contact British Transport Police if they have relevant information.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April regarding potential ties to Islamic State, and the West Yorkshire Police are currently investigating him and another missing teen, Hassan Munshi, who is the younger brother of a previous terrorism act convict.

The article announces that GB's ice hockey team, featuring three forwards and a goalie, will compete in a qualifying tournament against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia to reach the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang, with a significant overlap in players from the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning squad. Additionally, an Italian team, Cortina, will play against the Belfast Giants during the tournament in a first-time meeting between the clubs.

Matthew Perry may participate in a tribute to the show's creator, James Burrows, but it is not a reunion of the Friends cast as originally expected, with Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer, and Matt LeBlanc participating. The special will air on NBC on 21 February, and Friends ended in 2004. Matthew Perry is also set to star in a play titled The End of Longing in London's West End, running from 2 February until 14 May.

Veteran footballer Jones, who began his career at Manchester United and played for seven additional clubs including the Clarets where he aided in winning the Championship title last season, experienced the initial loss with his current team in the Premier League against Swansea on Saturday.

A renowned lawyer from Melbourne's Italian community, who had represented crime bosses accused of various offenses, was murdered, with authorities suspecting that underworld figures may have targeted him due to a potential bounty on his head, with renewed gangland tensions still present in Melbourne.

An Air France 777-200 en route from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland, due to a slight smell of burning on board, and a second aircraft was sent to transport passengers back to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

The Met Office has issued a severe weather warning, predicting strong winds and heavy rain as Hurricane Gonzalo reaches Britain on Monday night, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, with potentially damaging gusts exceeding 55mph inland and up to 70mph by exposed coastal areas, also canceling some Irish Ferries sailings between Holyhead and Dublin due to the weather forecast.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding, as told by Jenny, who spoke to a doctor in a children's hospital in Sheffield, and shared the experiences of patients Lilly and Jake, who had to wait extended periods due to overcrowding and subsequent wait times before being treated.

Alexander suffered a broken cheekbone in a victory over Rangers, potentially hindering his subsequent performances, while Lee Hollis, with experience at Motherwell, is being considered as a replacement for another Hearts goalkeeper, Neil, who is injured, with doubts surrounding his availability for the upcoming Edinburgh derby.

Her team Bucheon KEB Hana Bank faces annulment of records, league rule changes, and the departure of the owner and head coach due to this scandal.

The debris, marked with the UK Space Agency and Arianespace logos, likely originated from the launch vehicle payload shroud and is believed to have floated inland from the Atlantic. Rosie's Helping Hands, a charity founded in memory of 16-year-old Rosie Ross who was tragically killed in 2001, has raised £350,000 for young people's projects in Aldridge. Her parents, Karen and Ross, have decided to wind down the charity after the last annual Rosie's Walk event, as they feel the 16th anniversary next year will be an emotional milestone, and wish to move past the painful times while still continuing to fundraise for worthy causes. The charity has contributed to a new pirate-themed play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital, transforming a grey concrete space into a more welcoming and normalizing environment for sick children.

Macmillan Cancer Support plans to invest £5m in a new palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, aiming to provide inpatient, outpatient, and day care for incurable cancer and other conditions, ensuring easier access to specialist tests and treatments for patients in the county, and the unit is expected to open in late 2018 or early 2019.

The Columba Declaration, jointly authored by the Reverend John McPake and Bishop Peter Forster, aims to strengthen partnership and foster communion between the Church of Scotland and Church of England, allowing clergy and lay people to be welcomed in each other's church when moving across borders, and recognizing their separate constitutional responsibilities within the UK. The two Churches will debate the details of the agreement over the coming months.

British Army veteran Ben Parkinson, who was badly injured in a bomb attack in Afghanistan in 2006, received an overwhelming number of friend requests on Facebook during his torch-bearing run, reaching the 5,000 limit for personal pages. His mother Diane described the responses as "phenomenal," with thousands of people joining the Pilgrim Bandits website and offering support, firmly boosting Ben's morale.

The UN Agency for Human Settlements report indicates that income inequality in Latin America remains extremely high, with the richest 20% earning on average 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The study shows Guatemala as the country with the widest disparity, while Venezuela is the most equitable. The region is the world's most urbanized, with eight out of 10 people living in cities, and by 2050, nearly nine out of 10 Latin Americans will live in cities. The report suggests that during this period of relative economic stability and slower population growth, Latin American nations should prioritize making city life more equitable. The report also notes a considerable job deficit and a high rate of labor informality, particularly affecting young people and women. However, the UN Agency for Human Settlements' Erik Vittrup points to positive trends, such as a reduction in poverty, indigence, and unemployment in urban areas.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation after screenshots showed she shared a post from the far-right group Britain First advocating capital punishment for sex offenders, contradicting her opposition to the death penalty. The group, which initially aimed to raise £50,000, extended the target after reaching it in nine hours and is now fully funded to provide guidance on the possibility of successful legal action against key individuals involved in the invasion of Iraq.

Adnan Syed's legal team is reopening his case for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, after new evidence from the Serial podcast regarding mobile phone records and a potential alibi has been allowed by a judge. Asia McClain, a friend who claims to have seen Syed at a library during the time of the suspected crime, could serve as his alibi. The defense team will also challenge the prosecution's reliance on mobile phone records, claiming they were misleading and improperly admitted at trial.

A 16-year-old boy, who previously served custodial sentences for assaults at 14 and 15, pleaded guilty to assault after pulling a machete on a taxi driver during a return to a party in Dundee. Another 16-year-old boy admitted theft after stealing a bag containing the driver's change during the commotion. The court deferred sentences for both boys, pending social work background reports.

John Clancy, a Labour councillor for Quinton, was elected as the new leader of Birmingham City Council after five attempts, beating closest rival Penny Holbrook in a ballot by a single vote. Clancy, who previously taught English and had stints as a solicitor and business lecturer, aims to improve social housing, make smarter financial decisions, provide free school meals for all primary-age children, and expand regeneration outside the city centre. In an interview with Empire magazine ahead of the release of "Skyfall", actor Roger Moore discussed his early meetings with director Guy Hamilton and his approach to avoiding deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery in portraying James Bond, while producer Barbara Broccoli highlighted how Connery's unconventional portrayal of Bond had broken traditional class structures, with inputfrom dance teacher Yat Malmgren and scriptwriter Terence Young on Connery's appearance and demeanor.

Witches' marks, carvings believed to provide protection against witches and evil spirits during the medieval era, have been found in various historical structures such as Shakespeare's birthplace and Tower of London, and Historic England aims to encourage documenting these symbols during Halloween, as significant records about their occurrence and types are scarce.

The decision affects thousands of passengers who had claims against Jet2, Thomas Cook, Ryanair, and WizzAir, arising from the EU regulations that oblige airlines to pay compensation for cancellations and delays, unless extraordinary circumstances are involved.

Several nations, including China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei, claim territory in the resource-rich region, making it a potential flashpoint with global consequences.

The Co-op Bank, known for its ethical stance and having four million customers, has announced that its recapitalization plan with existing investors is substantially agreed, aiming to alleviate its financial struggles and satisfy Bank of England regulations, despite still carrying a share of the Co-operative Group's £8bn pension liabilities.

While NRW claims its figures of a 21% death rate for salmon and 25% for sea trout are based on the best available evidence, TLP disputes these numbers, stating that their own modeling estimates a "worst case scenario" of 2% of all fish species dying. The UK government is currently reviewing the viability of the project, and both NRW and TLP are calling for clarity on the government's position.

The BBC, in collaboration with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to select and operate the iPlayer on-demand platform by concentrating or relaxing their minds, with potential applications in assisting people with disabilities and expanding the use of brainwave technology in controlling electronic devices.

The Welsh Government recognizes the need to support and challenge their most able students, and are implementing changes to the school performance measurement system and introducing programs to extend opportunities for all young people.

The unreleased 1981 and 1984 recordings by Johnny Cash, featuring duets with his wife June Carter and friend Waylon Jennings, titled "Out Among the Stars", will be released in March, posthumously. The recordings, featuring 12 tracks, were found gathering dust in a vault in 2012 and have never been made public before. Carter Cash maintains the release is worthwhile for fans and compares it to discovering an unseen Picasso, given Cash's immense success (over 90 million records sold) and his history of reaching out to underrepresented audiences.

The court of appeal dismissed the Ardoyne Association's appeal. McKeith was awarded compensation of £10,000 for injury to feelings, £6,760 for loss of earnings, and £2,126 in interest. Employers are reminded to recognize their obligations under the Disability Discrimination Act, particularly in regard to treating disabled individuals and their primary carers with dignity and respect.

Scottish midfielder Kenny McLean Dorrans, after being rejected in two bids by Norwich City, signed a three-year deal with Rangers, becoming Pedro Caixinha's ninth summer signing, joining the likes of Bruno Alves, Daniel Candeias, Carlos Pena, Eduardo Herrera, Dalcio, Ryan Jack, Alfredo Morelos, and Fabio Cardoso, and expressing excitement to start his journey at Ibrox.

Team Brewster clinched the men's spot for the European Championships by defeating David Murdoch's Olympic silver medallist team, while Eve Muirhead's rink secured the women's spot with three wins in a best-of-five tournament final. Muirhead, who is the sister of skip Glen Muirhead, and her team look forward to competing in the Championships in their home country, while teammate Anna Sloan is set for her return from injury.

Councillor Pierre Oxley has called a scrutiny meeting regarding a beach defense project, accusing the project leader Peter Halliday of scaremongering, while Halliday asserts that the council has been transparent and that the percentage of sand and shingle in the beach recharge is clear in project reports. The meeting is scheduled for next Tuesday.

John Nelms announced a land use application will be submitted for land in Camperdown Park, partly due to financial issues: an operating loss of £530,000, increased wages, and higher maintenance costs for the aging stadium, despite investments exceeding £200,000. The plan is to enhance Dundee Football Club with a land use application near the city's Ice Arena.

Chris Froome, the Team Sky rider, finished second at the Criterium du Dauphine stage two behind winner Jesus Herrada of Movistar. Alberto Contador (Tinkoff) currently leads the overall standings, six seconds ahead of Richie Porte (BMC Racing), with Froome 13 seconds behind Contador in third place. Froome will prioritize the Tour de France and Olympic road race in Rio, as he was not included in the list of athletes competing for the British Championships.

The ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake, 43, and her sons, Zachary, 8, and Amon, 4, were found dead in their home on Tuesday, and the case is now being treated as a triple murder inquiry. The police are seeking Arthur Simpson-Kent, the partner of Sian, who has reportedly left the UK and travelled to Ghana. The Met police's handling of the case is being investigated by the IPCC following earlier concerns about Sian's welfare, with significant attempts made to conceal the bodies found in the garden during excavations on Tuesday.

Due to multiple match interruptions, Wimbledon organizers have decided to play tennis matches on the traditional rest day (middle Sunday) for the first time since 2004, with at least eight guaranteed singles' matches to be played, and further details to be released on Saturday.

Dutch manager Dick Advocaat, who steered relegation-threatened Sunderland to safety last season, has decided to leave the club after less than a year, citing a commitment to his wife and foregoing any financial settlement. His departure marks a trend set by previous managers Gus Poyet and Paolo di Canio, who also arrived to save Sunderland from relegation and left the following season. The club, currently without a win in their first eight league matches of the 2015-16 season, has seen little success under Advocaat, with only one winthis season against League Two side Exeter in the League Cup.

Russia anticipates a 0.8% GDP decline next year, due to the combined effects of an oil price slump, Western sanctions primarily aimed at oil and gas industries, banks, arms manufacturers and elites, and a weakened rouble (losing half its value in 2014) that impacts various sectors such as manufacturing, construction, agriculture, and services, except energy, mining, and retail trade. To combat the economic downturn, President Putin utilizes measures like increasing bank deposit guarantees and providing soft loans to banks, particularly Sberbank.

Opposition leader Raila Odinga is challenging the 2017 Kenyan presidential election results in court, accusing the electoral authorities of fraud and rigging, while foreign observers describe the election as free and fair. The international community is urging calm amid fears of potential violence, and Odinga insists this is not a concession but a pursuit for justice for voters and a test of the Supreme Court's independence.

A 60-year-old man dies while scuba diving at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland, following two French tourists' deaths due to cardiac arrests while snorkeling on a nearby reef just days prior. The incident occurred on a tour boat with safety equipment, including oxygen and defibrillation equipment, but resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. The man was travelling with his wife and the tour operator has expressed sympathy for the tragic event.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have collectively agreed on a 3.7 million-pound contract to continue the Dundee-London Stansted route, operated by Loganair, for two more years. The UK Government's contribution is 50% through the Regional Air Connectivity Fund, while the Scottish government and Dundee City Council put in 1.4 million pounds and 400,000 pounds respectively. The route will offer two return flights daily and one on Sunday.

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is launching its video streaming service in China, making its part-sport, part soap-opera content available in the world's largest potential customer base. Success in China will depend on finding local stars and competition is intense, but past events have received a great response, and Chinese stars could be key to capitalizing on the market's vast size.

Three men, including a police officer, are being questioned by West Midlands Police over allegations of conspiring to pervert the course of justice and misconduct in a public office, after providing false and malicious information suggesting a terrorist kidnap plot, which led to the force going on high alert and officers being advised to avoid wearing uniforms.

Ireland defeated Poland 5-1 in a crucial quarter-final match, with key contributions from McKee (2 goals), Eugene Magee, and O'Donoghue (2 goals). The victory sets up a semi-final against Wales on Saturday, with the winner advancing to the final and World League 3. Ireland's coach Craig Fulton praised his team's performance, particularly their pressure on Poland and the areas they were winning the ball. Poland's standout player was Mateusz Poltaszewski.

Philip Craig, a 38-year-old man from Leeds, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for the murder of Christopher Laskaris, a 24-year-old man with Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in November. Craig exploited Laskaris, supplying him with drugs, and killed him with a single stab wound to the heart. Craig returned to the flat where the body remained to steal more possessions, including a TV, games console, and guitars. Laskaris' family stated that his death had a "devastating impact" and that nothing could ever heal their pain and loss. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, who was also charged with the murder, had his case discharged in February.

The police have closed the reinvestigation into the death of Kester David, a former police informant who was found burned under a bridge in 2010, and apologized for initial failures to properly investigate; the Met Commissioner Sir Bernard Hogan-Howe admitted to a "catalogue of errors" and insensitivity towards David's family, and concluded there was no evidence of a third party's involvement in his death.

In 2015, football was the most attended sport in the UK with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union attendances rose to 7.5 million due to the World Cup. Wimbledon remained the most popular individual event with nearly half a million spectators. Horseracing saw record attendance of 6.2 million, with names like Royal Ascot, Cheltenham Festival, and Epsom Derby in the top tier. Two new events entered the top 10 - MotoGP's British Grand Prix and the Badminton Horse Trials. Overall, attendance fell short of the 2012 record, but with a 6% rise without one-off events like the Olympic Games and Rugby World Cup. Major sports in 2016 included UCI Track Cycling World Championships, European Aquatics Championships, and FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list of highest-earning music artists, accumulating an estimated $105 million (£66 million) in 2013-2014, with Taylor Swift following closely in second at $64 million (£40 million), Pink at third with $52 million (£32.5 million), Rihanna at fourth with $48 million (£30 million), and Katy Perry at fifth with $40 million (£25 million). The earnings were calculated from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures between June 2013 and June 2014, featuring data from organizations such as Nielsen SoundScan. Other notable artists that failed to make the top 10 include Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys.

In the article, the Scottish National Party (SNP) claims that it has more support among MPs than Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, citing the loss of two-thirds of Labour's shadow cabinet and its inability to fill key shadow post roles. Labour, however, is currently recognized as the official opposition, with Corbyn maintaining power despite a no-confidence vote. The SNP argues it could fill all relevant government shadow posts, while Labour has yet to appoint a shadow Scottish secretary.

Villagers in Crickhowell have successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange, which was initially halted by Punch Taverns, aiming to turn it into independent shops with flats above. A new company, Corn Exchange Crickhowell Ltd, will be set up to secure planning permission, with around 180 people becoming joint-owners upon signing the deal.

Alliance Trust will continue with a strategic review that may lead to a sale or outsourcing, and will halt its practice of buying shares on the stock exchange until the review is complete; RIT Capital, after initial talks, will not make a formal bid for Alliance Trust.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking passengers in April 2013 into believing they had too much cash when boarding flights, resulting in them giving her money under false pretext. Judge James Mahoney recognized the "persistent, planned, and subtle" nature of her crimes, noting the severe impact on public trust and the international reputation of the country. The victims lost approximately £13,500, which Sussex Police later repaid.

The educational platform TrueTube, along with Horrible Histories and various other productions, have been nominated across multiple categories in upcoming Bafta Children's Awards, with TrueTube's works being recognized for their impact on young audiences' media consumption patterns. The winners will be announced on 20th November at the Roundhouse in London.

Lady Mary Soames, the last surviving child of Sir Winston Churchill, allocated most of her late father's artwork to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. The paintings include Lady Soames' favorites - Coast Scene near Cannes (1935) and View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club, 1946. This selection for the nation includes Churchill's work alongside a painting by Sir John Lavery and the Aly Khan Gold Cup, honoring the political and artistic legacy of this historical figure.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for allegedly stealing sensitive security documents, which police and MI5 believe could endanger lives. The documents don't relate to any current investigation by the ombudsman's office. The police have launched a criminal investigation and have temporarily halted the sharing of sensitive material with the ombudsman's office until a review of security protocols is conducted. Both the Police Federation and Ulster Unionist MP are calling for an independent investigation into the matter due to concerns about the office's integrity.

Phyllis Schlafly, a staunch conservative and outspoken opponent of feminism and abortion, played a pivotal role in the 1970s by blocking the Equal Rights Amendment and is credited as a key figure that contributed to the rise of Ronald Reagan, dedicating her life to traditional family values, and her legacy was affirmed by Donald Trump's endorsement before her death.

Professional rugby player Aled Morgan, 23, will leave Bristol at the end of the season, choosing to move back to Wales to further his career development and aim for a place in the Welsh national team. He has attracted interest from several clubs, including Newport Gwent Dragons, and can play at full-back or fly-half. His move to Bristol in 2014 resulted from limited game-time at fly-half for the Ospreys due to competition from Dan Biggar and Sam Davies.

The article reports that Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad were found not guilty of causing the death of three-year-old Syrian refugee Alan Kurdi through deliberate negligence, but convicted of people smuggling, while the image of Alan lying dead on a Turkish beach focused global attention on the refugee crisis in September 2015, and his family, including his five-year-old brother and mother, also drowned during an attempted boat crossing to Greece.

Former member of the CIA, Robert Lady, was released and boarded a U.S.-bound flight after serving a nine-year sentence for his involvement in the 2003 abduction of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar, who was allegedly subjected to torture. This case, known as the "extraordinary rendition" of Abu Omar, was the first trial involving such practices, which have been widely condemned for violating international agreements. In 2009, 22 CIA agents including Lady were convicted in absentia for their role in the abduction, but none have ever appeared in an Italian court.

Scottish airports reported significant increases in passenger numbers for January 2017, with Edinburgh leading the pack at 11.7%, followed by Glasgow at 8.4%, and Aberdeen experiencing its lowest decline in two years. International flights showed the most significant growth in Edinburgh and Glasgow, while domestic traffic showed a minor increase. Helicopter traffic declined in Aberdeen due to inclement weather conditions and a maintenance recall. Notably, Ryanair announced plans to extend its Aberdeen schedule with new flights to Faro and the Faroe Islands.
YouTube has increased the maximum view limit for videos from 2,147,483,647 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,808, after Gangnam Style by Psy surpassed the old limit.

England, after losing to West Indies and recovering from a poor performance against Afghanistan, aim to win against Sri Lanka to secure a place in the World Twenty20 semi-finals for the second time since its inception in 2007. The defending champions, Sri Lanka, are struggling with their batting but remain a formidable opponent due to their quality spinners, having defeated England in their last T20 match.

Scotland's largest cities, Edinburgh and Glasgow, rank second and third respectively in Britain's most congested cities, with estimated losses of £2.8bn and £2.3bn for Edinburgh and Glasgow respectively over the next decade due to traffic jams. The UK-wide total for wasted time in traffic jams is projected to reach £61.8bn by 2025 if congestion levels persist without intervention, according to a study by Inrix Roadway Analytics. London is not only the worst-affected city in the UK in terms of congestion, but also has more traffic "pinch points" than any other city in Europe and ranks worst in an assessment of the impact of its traffic jams. The researchers suggest identifying traffic hotspots and analyzing their root causes as a key strategy for addressing the issue of congestion.

In a friendly match, Norway scored three goals, with standout contributors Elyounoussi, Ruud, and Nordtveit, while Northern Ireland struggled to find their stride and managed only a single goal chance, firmly losing 0-3.

Authorities in Belgium maintain high alert levels as intelligence suggests potential Paris-style attacks due to one Paris gunman once residing there. Abdelhamid Abaaoud, the suspected ringleader of the Paris attacks, was near the Bataclan theatre and had allegedly returned to targeted cafes, with evidence of planning an attack on the La Defense business district. A man named Mohamed Abrini, believed to have driven a car with Salah Abdeslam, a wanted man after the attacks, to a Paris-bound motorway petrol station, is currently being sought as dangerous and possibly armed by Belgian authorities.

A series of coordinated bombings occurred on March 22, 2016 at Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels, leading to 31 deaths and numerous injuries. The Belgian authorities declared three days of national mourning and service disruptions, with Prime Minister Charles Michel calling for unity. Some suspect links to the November 2015 Paris attacks have been proposed, and US President Barack Obama offered assistance in the investigation.

Local Green Party councillor Alison Teal has received a legal warning from Sheffield City Council, threatening an injunction for her part in protests against the council's tree felling program. The council maintains the removals are lawful and necessary, citing unlawful disruptions to tree replacement works by a small number of protesters. The council supports peaceful protests but will take action against those engaging in direct action causing work disruptions, as the Street Ahead program aims to improve the city's street scene and street tree stock for the next 25 years.

In one of the worst whale stranding incidents in New Zealand's history, over 400 whales have stranded themselves at Farewell Spit, South Island, with approximately 300 deaths reported. Local residents and conservation department staff are working together to refloat the survivors, often forming human chains, while scientists continue to investigate the causes of whale stranding events. Farewell Spit, known for its shallow waters, is often cited as a location where the whales mistakenly navigate, leading to many such incidents. New Zealand has one of the highest rates of whale and dolphin strandings worldwide, with around 300 incidents occurring annually.

The Welsh rugby club Ospreys have signed 32-year-old scrummager Brian Mujati as injury cover for Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, with Rhodri Jones currently on international duty. Mujati, who has experience playing in Super Rugby, Top 14, and English Premiership, is expected to add valuable experience and help the team navigate through the remaining PRO12 games and the Challenge Cup quarter-final.

The Gwynedd council proceeds to establish a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite opposition from 500 community members and concerns about trust from the governors of the schools involved.

According to the article, Oxfordshire County Council proposed a plan to save £100m over five years by merging all services under one organization, while district councils prefer three councils and an elected mayor, with each side accusing the other of prioritizing bureaucracy over service provision. The county council insists the change is necessary due to the necessity of cuts to local services, while the district councils argue that an elected mayor would provide a stronger voice to Oxford and increase funding from central government. Residents are being consulted on the proposals prior to the county council's cabinet meeting on 14 March.

Edinburgh rugby team, with Dickinson, Nel, and Ford in the starting front row, must win five tough upcoming matches, starting against Newport Gwent Dragons, to have a chance at playoff or top six finish. Per Dickinson, they've struggled with errors and soft tries, but have focused on improving minor details to turn things around.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group is rescuing grounded and injured bats that have been found in unusual places due to the poor summer weather conditions, which have affected the bats' mothers' ability to feed and produce milk. Volunteers such as Karen Healy are caring for the bats in their homes, nursing them back to health with a focus on their wing recuperation and flight capacity, before releasing them back into the wild. Healy emphasizes the positive impact bats have on the economy, particularly in agricultural pest control, and debunks common misconceptions about them, such as their blood-drinking or blindness.

The Supreme Court is deliberating on whether to expand limitations on the federal law that prevents gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, as highlighted by Justice Thomas' recent questioning regarding the potential suspension of constitutional rights due to law violations. This comes following Justice Thomas' previous silence in court, attributed to his belief in private conversations with fellow justices and his preference for not questioning lawyers unless he seeks an answer.

Responsible Travel, a wildlife holiday specialist, has decided to drop about half a dozen tours that involve traditional zoos from their selection of 3,500 trips, after their CEO, Justin Francis, deemed them outdated and inhumane, citing inadequatejustifications for animal captivity and limited successful reintroduction of endangered species to the wild. The decision was supported by wildlife charity, Born Free Foundation, which expressed concerns about the impact of captivity on animal welfare and behavior.

A 40-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder after police discovered the body of a primary-school-aged child in Faringdon, England. Police have stepped up their presence in the area as a means of providing reassurance, while local residents expressed shock and sadness following the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.

A suspect is accused of breaching the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim) for not contacting a monitoring company and reporting to a police station in January, marking what is allegedly the first such breach case. The defendant, who can't be named, was granted bail and a hearing date was set for July, while additional details about the case were withheld by the Home Office.

Qualcomm, the major supplier of chips for smartphones, has agreed to lower royalty rates on patents in China's mobile phone market, a move that could benefit domestic companies like Xiaomi and Huawei, following a ruling that Qualcomm violated China's anti-monopoly law. This change could potentially boost Qualcomm's revenue in China's expanding high-speed 4G network market, as it makes up about half of its global revenue.

In the article, it is detailed that Michelle Mellotte, a former doctor, was found guilty of fraud by abusing her role by taking £10,000 from a patient with Alzheimer's, promising to return it that summer. In 2014, Mellotte received a suspended prison sentence and was suspended from the medical register. Last week, the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service in Manchester determined that Mellotte put patients at risk, brought the profession into disrepute and breached fundamental tenets of the profession. As a result, she is no longer able to practice as a doctor in the UK.

A nearly complete male skeleton, aged between 30 and 49, was found at the bottom of an embankment near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, UK, around 2-3 years ago. The remains were wearing contemporary clothing and investigators are unable to rule out potential criminal activity, as they continue to investigate the cause of death.

The archaeological discovery of a 30m square of megaliths, previously hidden and buried within the Avebury circles, is deemed a "great surprise" and considered one of the earliest structures at the site. It is speculated that this stone square could have been used to commemorate and monumentalize the ancestral home of the first people living in Avebury, potentially offering insights into the motivation behind building the extensive Avebury monument complex.

The article discusses an opposition to a parking scheme proposal in Reading by hospital staff and residents, arguing that the implementation of pay and display meters could exacerbate parking pressures around the hospital and university areas, thus presenting challenges for staff, patients, and local residents.

US Navy's Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, in a recent three-car accident in Okinawa, was drinking six times over the legal limit and had her liberty curtailed by the US military due to her actions, stoking ongoing resentment among Okinawans who oppose the heavy military presence and the latest crime committed by the service members.

In a highly successful tri-series, England's Lions, coached by former England captain Andrew Flower, displayed impressive batting performances, with Ben Duckett scoring the ninth-highest List A score ever (220 not out) and Zak Crawley making 171, to comfortably beat Sri Lanka A twice and Pakistan A twice, while Dawid Malan (185) and Sam Billings (175) also excelled. Flower praised the young talent and predicted that the selectors will take note of their performances.

Colombia's peace talks with the FARC rebels, mediated by Cuba and Norway, are resuming on 10 December following the release of three hostages. The discussions will focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victim's family concerns, with additional talks scheduled for mid-January. The negotiations, which began in 2012, aim to end a five-decade-long conflict that has resulted in an estimated 220,000 deaths.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign led a protest against Oxfordshire County Council's plan to close 44 children's centers and replace them with eight, aiming to save £8m. Former Prime Minister David Cameron was invited to join the protest, and the PM's office responded by stating there is still scope for savings across local government.

A controversial sandcastle depicting a murder victim in a suggestive manner, entered by Devon and Cornwall Police, won a beach games competition but drew criticism for being offensive, trivializing serious matters, and containing sexual stereotypes. The police apologized for any offense caused.

Slade, Leyton Orient's football manager, discusses a proposed shift in the club's structure due to a new owner's takeover, emphasizing his focus on football matters and the need for improved team performance, while noting the learning curve involved for both parties due to the owner's lack of football club experience.

Tyrrell Hatton secured a spot at the USPGA Championship, booked a place at The Open Championship for the fifth time in six years, and earned his largest career payday at the Scottish Open, despite finishing a shot behind the victorious Alex Noren. Despite slipping away a few birdie chances on the back nine, Hatton maintains a positive outlook, eyeing a strong performance at The Open, particularly focusing on making it through to the weekend.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse Many Clouds, known for his successful races including the Cotswold Chase and the Hennessy Gold Cup, suffered a severe pulmonary haemorrhage and collapsed after a race, despite having no significant underlying health issues, and his death remains a rare and unexplained incident in horse racing.

A woman testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was 12 when she was picked up from a children's home, abused, and taken to Blackpool where she was forced to work and raped daily by several men, including Basharat Hussain, who denies the allegations. He and six others, including Karen MacGregor, Shelley Davies, Arshid Hussain, Qurban Ali, Majid Bostan, and Sajid Bostan, are on trial for child abuse, including rape, in Rotherham, with prosecutors claiming they targeted, sexualized, and subjected children to degrading and violent acts between 1987 and 2003.

A 32-year-old racer, Franck Petricola, tragically lost his life after making his comeback at the TT following a serious accident at the North West 200 in 2014. The racing community expresses deep sympathy for his family and friends following the incident, and an investigation is underway regarding the circumstances leading to his death.

The Honda Racing team has announced that Guy Martin will not be returning to the Isle of Man TT due to his crash in June and the team's mechanical issues this year, although the competition at this year's event is expected to be strong, with impressive performances from Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, and Dean Harrison.

President Barack Obama has declared a state of disaster in Louisiana due to severe flooding caused by torrential rain, affecting over 20,000 people, many of whom are still trapped in their homes, with some needing to be rescued from their homes or boats. The floods have caused extensive damage and have been considered as a flood of "epic proportions" comparable to the disaster caused by Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

In the article, US Soccer settles a lawsuit filed by parents on behalf of young soccer players who accused the federation of negligence regarding concussions. As part of the settlement, US Soccer has resolved to limit the amount of heading in practice for children aged 11 to 13 and introduce new safety measures, including changes to substitution rules for concussions and guidelines for managing head injuries. The Football Association in England is also working on new guidelines regarding head injuries and their long-term effects on the brain.

Former president Nicolas Sarkozy was not aware of the falsification of 11 million euros worth of invoices during his 2012 campaign, according to Jerome Lavrilleux, a deputy director of Sarkozy's campaign. The allegations were made by Bygmalion's lawyer, Patrick Maisonneuve, who claimed that the UMP ordered these invoices to cover campaign costs. The scandal could potentially harm Sarkozy's chances of being re-elected and challenge Jean-Francois Cope's leadership of the UMP party due to the growing speculation about the party's payments to Bygmalion.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders reported a decrease in home repossessions (2,500) from Q1 and Q2 of the previous year (5,400), with 1,800 homes repossessed from owner-occupiers and 700 from landlords. Low interest rates were cited as a significant contributing factor. However, a potential increase in interest rates was highlighted as a future concern for homeowners, with the CML encouraging prompt action for those encountering difficulties. Additionally, the number of tenants evicted by landlords rose by 4% compared to the same period last year, contributing to thousands of families losing their homes, according to Shelter's chief executive.

The article describes that Coventry City Council accepted 105 Syrian refugees from October 2018 to March 2019 as part of the UK Government's expanded resettlement program. The council stated that all associated costs are covered by the Government, and UKIP MEP James Carver criticized Coventry for taking more refugees than other areas, arguing that the pressure on services should be distributed fairly. The Home Office commended the goodwill shown by the 71 local authorities involved in the program so far. The Government committed to resettling 20,000 Syrian refugees by 2020, spending approximately £500 million. The West Midlands region, particularly Birmingham and Stafford, received the majority of the refugees, with 159 Syrians settled in the area. The North West region did not accept any refugees, while 33 were placed in London and only three in Kingston upon Thames and Mid Sussex. Coventry City Council deputy leader Abdul Khan defended the decision to accept refugees with significant medical needs and affected by the violence in Syria.

Brazil's president, Ms. Rousseff, declares her confidence in organizing a safe and successful Olympic Games in 2016, with the Olympic torch relay starting in May and passing through 300 Brazilian cities before culminating at Rio's Maracana stadium at the opening ceremony. She also allays concerns over security, delays, and water pollution, insisting that the upcoming Games will be historic, marking the first time a South American city hosts the Olympics.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's reform guarantees a majority of seats to the party that wins the most votes in an election, seeking to end the country's legacy of unstable coalitions. Critics, however, argue that the law consolidates power, as it awards too much power to single parties and denies direct voter representation.

The 20-year-old Ajax player Abdelhak Nouri suffered severe brain damage due to a lack of oxygen supply during a game, as revealed by new tests, with chances of recovery being nil, according to the club statement.

Swansea earned a crucial victory after falling behind against Aston Villa, with Gylfi Sigurdsson's free-kick and Andre Ayew's late goal turning the match around. The win, while difficult after a six-game winless streak, enhances team morale and provides confidence ahead of the upcoming game against Arsenal.

Mani Dad, a boy living with his Polish mother Leyla Dad in Kielce, Poland, is believed to be with his British father Zayn Dean in the UK. Leyla launching family court proceedings, has asked Costa coffee shops customers to look out for Mani and his father, as they are believed to frequent these places. The family once lived in England before moving to Poland. Leyla, who is now in Poland, expressed concern for Mani's welfare and is seeking his return.

U.S. authorities have changed travel rules for individuals with dual citizenship from certain countries, including Iran, under a visa waiver program, leading to confusion and frustration, as seen in the case of BBC Persian presenter Rana Rahimpour, who was prevented from traveling due to her Iranian nationality.
